outcome.description: The outcome, in the source's own words.

facts.description: The facts it read after spending, where it read them.

FactsReport.description: The members of a provider's facts this read tells. A member present, even null or [], is told by this read; a member absent is not told and keeps what was told before. Members of a later contract are ignored.

identity.description: Who the credential belongs to, at most 200 characters.

credential.description: How the credential was given, what it is, and when it lapses.

credential_verified.description: True only where this read authenticated with the provider's credential; it is kept only from a read that was given the key.

plan.description: The plan's id, at most 200 characters; the name shown for it is the one the source's `plans` give.

windows.description: The usage windows of the plan, at most 64, each by its `id`: how much is used in percent, and when it starts over.

limit_reached.description: A limit of the plan that has been reached, with when it lifts: new turns wait until then, or until a read admits ordinary use.

ordinary_usage_allowed.description: Whether the vendor admits ordinary use now: false holds new turns, true lifts that.

balances.description: What is left to be spent, at most 32, each by its `id` and in its own unit; amounts are decimal text.

spend.description: What has been spent over periods, at most 64, each by its `id`, with the period's limit where it has one; amounts are decimal text.

extra_usage.description: Spending beyond the plan, in the vendor's unit.

available_resets.description: The resets that can be spent, with their credits, at most 64; a source that spends them declares `spends_resets`.

method.description: A sign-in method's id; `null` for a key.

expires_at.description: When a token lapses, where that is known.

issued_at.description: When the credential was issued, where its own claims say so.

CredentialFacts.description: How a provider was given its credential, and when it lapses.

oneOf.description: A token used as it is.

CredentialYield.description: What a credential yields, as a provider's facts say it.

id.description: The vendor's id for the window.

duration_minutes.description: How long it is, in minutes; `null` where it has no fixed length.

used_percent.description: How much of it is used, from 0 to 100. A vendor may report a fraction.

model_family.description: The family of models this window covers; null means the whole plan.

is_active.description: Whether the vendor marks this as the binding window.

reset_not_started.description: The source reports an unstarted or not yet fixed reset, distinct from an unknown reset.

warning_percent.description: The vendor's warning mark, in percent, where it names one.

severity.description: The vendor's severity for display, without a notification.

UsageWindow.description: How much of a usage window of the vendor's plan is used.

type.description: Which limit, as the vendor names it.

LimitReached.description: A limit of the plan that has been reached.

id.description: The source's name for it, one of a kind among the balances it tells: `plan`, `account`, a currency.

label.description: What it is called for people, where the source names it.

unit.description: The vendor's unit: a currency such as `USD` or `CNY`, or `credits`.

used.description: What has been spent of it.

parts.description: What it is made of, where the vendor splits it.

expires_at.description: When it lapses, where it does.

Balance.description:
What an account, a plan or a key still holds to be spent, in the vendor's own unit: not Orch's credits.

Amounts are decimal text (`"12.50"`), so that the vendor's precision is kept as it was told.

label.description: What the vendor calls the part.

amount.description: How much it is, as decimal text in the balance's unit.

BalancePart.description: One part of a balance, where the vendor splits it, such as what was granted and what was topped up.

id.description: The source's name for the row, one of a kind among the rows it tells.

label.description: What it is called for people, where the source names it.

period_minutes.description: For a period of its own length, how long it is, in minutes.

used.description: What has been spent in the period.

limit.description: The most that may be spent in it.

remaining.description: What is left of the limit.

Spend.description:
What has been spent over one period, in the vendor's own unit, and the limit of that period where there
is one. Amounts are decimal text.

oneOf.description: A day, by the vendor's clock.
A week, by the vendor's clock.
A month, by the vendor's clock.
A window of its own length, given as `period_minutes`.

SpendPeriod.description: The period a row of spending covers.

used.description: What has been used, where known.

used_percent.description: How much is used, in percent.

unit.description: The vendor's currency or unit, where supplied.

decimal_places.description: The scale the vendor uses for its amounts.

disabled_reason.description: Why it is disabled, when the vendor says.

limit_reached.description: Whether its spending limit is reached.

ExtraUsage.description: Spending beyond a subscription's included plan, in the vendor's unit.

available_count.description: The count, which may be greater than the detail list's length.

credits.description: Null means only the count is known; an empty list means no details were returned.

AvailableResets.description: How many resets are available and the detail rows the vendor supplied.

description.description: What the vendor says the reset begins anew.

reset_type.description: The type of reset, in the vendor's vocabulary.

status.description: Whether the vendor says it is available, redeeming, redeemed or unknown.

expires_at.description: When it lapses, or null when it has no known end.

ResetCredit.description: One reset credit as the vendor lists it.
